claim: Retail traders lost about $358,000 per day on SPX 0DTE options after daily expirations began 16 May 2022 (about $184,000 per day over the full roughly two-year sample); about 60% of daily losses came from transaction costs.
quote: since May 16, 2022 (the introduction of a daily expiration calendar), daily retail losses grew to $358,000. About 60% of daily losses were the result of transaction costs
title: Retail Investors are in Love with Same Day Options (coverage of Beckmeyer, Branger, Gayda 2023)

claim: Delta-hedged long S&P 500 index option positions underperform zero on average; underperformance is smaller for options away from the money and larger when volatility is high (Bakshi and Kapadia, RFS 2003). This is delta-hedged, not outright long, and the sample is old.
quote: First, the delta-hedged strategy underperforms zero. Second, the documented underperformance is less for options away from the money. Third, the underperformance is greater at times of higher volatility.
title: Delta-Hedged Gains and the Negative Market Volatility Risk Premium (abstract, RePEc)

claim: An IVolatility backtest of S&P 500 earnings straddles reports aggregate long-straddle expectancy of -18.5% per trade with 22% win rate, with an average IV crush of 15.6 percentage points (vendor self-reported).
quote: Aggregate long-straddle expectancy across the index is −18.5% per trade with 22% WR , driven by an average IV crush of +15.6pp
title: Does IVolAI's Earnings Edge Actually Pay? Stress-Testing 9,622 Real S&P 500 Straddles

claim: Option Alpha found implied volatility contracted after about 90% of earnings events in a sample of 1,546 events (vendor self-reported).
quote: This means that about 90% of the time we saw implied volatility go through a crush or contraction.
title: We stopped trading earnings after we saw this new research (Option Alpha)

claim: FlashAlpha's 7-year backtest of short put spreads (not long options) shows the result depends on the fill model: honest fills give breakeven to negative, mid fills give strongly positive; this is a general warning about mid-price backtests.
quote: honest fills give breakeven to negative (these numbers); idealized mid-fills (the universal public-backtest default) give strongly positive.
title: VRP Short Put Spreads: Honest 7-Year Backtest, 5 Symbols (FlashAlpha)

claim: ORATS' covered-call backtest (selling calls, not buying) found 30 DTE, 10 delta, avoiding earnings and holding to expiration most profitable; it does not test long options and does not transfer to the buy-side practices.
quote: selling calls with 30 days to expiration and 10 delta, avoiding earnings, and holding to expiration were the most profitable strategies.
title: Covered call backtest: finding the best maturity, strike, IV and earnings methods (ORATS)

claim: A practitioner estimates 0.05-0.3% slippage per trade, so a strategy trading 30 times a month loses 1-2% a month to slippage (generic algo-trading post, not options-specific, unverified estimate).
